_readme: TOML. The third format, and the one where a reserialise would do the most damage: Codex keeps
model settings, plugin toggles, project trust levels and MCP servers in ONE file. A repair
that reformats the document rewrites configuration it was never asked to touch.
The inputs below are shaped after the real ~/.codex/config.toml read on 2026-08-22: table
syntax, comments, blank-line spacing and unrelated sections around the target. The unrelated
sections are the point — they must come back byte-identical.
Fix expectations describe the target for step 3. This client is not write-capable yet: its
remote-HTTP field names are documented rather than captured.

cases.name: healthy
cases.description: A correct remote entry sitting beside unrelated configuration.

raw_files..codex/config.toml:
model = "gpt-5.6-terra"
model_reasoning_effort = "high"

[mcp_servers.superdocs]
url = "https://api.superdocs.app/mcp"

[mcp_servers.superdocs.http_headers]
Authorization = "Bearer sk_fixture_toml_healthy_0"

[projects."/Users/dev/work"]
trust_level = "trusted"

cases.name: scheme-insecure
cases.description: http:// on the canonical host, with unrelated tables above and below.

cases._why: The comment, the blank lines, the sibling key and both unrelated tables survive verbatim. One word changes.

cases.name: auth-header-no-bearer
cases.description: A key in the header table without the Bearer scheme.

cases.name: stdio-server
cases.description: A command-based entry, the shape actually observed in the live config. Out of scope, named rather than ignored.
cases._why: Both MCP servers in the real config were this shape, so it is the likeliest thing the tool will meet in a Codex file.

cases.name: no-entry-among-other-servers
cases.description: Other MCP servers configured, none of them SuperDocs.

raw_files..codex/config.toml:
model = "gpt-5.6-terra"

[mcp_servers.node_repl]
command = "/usr/local/bin/node-repl"
args = []

[mcp_servers.computer-use]
command = "/usr/local/bin/computer-use"
args = ["mcp"]
enabled = false

cases._why: Modelled on the real file, which had exactly these two stdio servers. Other people's servers must be left completely alone.

cases.name: host-rule-gateway
cases.description: The host rule in TOML: an entry pointing at a policy gateway is left byte-identical.

raw_files..codex/config.toml:
# routed via the platform gateway
[mcp_servers.superdocs]
url = "http://localhost:8080/mcp"

[mcp_servers.superdocs.http_headers]
Authorization = "Bearer gw_fixture_toml_team_000"

cases.name: invalid-toml
cases.description: A broken TOML file is never auto-rewritten.
cases._why: An unclosed table header. Repairing a file we could not parse would mean guessing at the structure of a document holding this user's project trust levels.
